boundaries.evidence: Definition clauses(b)–(d) require nonempty S, Theta, Z and N>=1,d>=1, so record boxes contain their centers. Clause(a) does not impose r>=1 on the finite run-description tuple; an empty tuple introduces no measured quantity or prediction. Operational use still owes the explicit interpretation condition(*), rather than deriving a reading from tuple structure.

The Definition admits zero throughout: $\varepsilon_k$ may be $0$, making the declared box the singleton $\{z_k\}$; clause (e) admits the total declared bound $B=0$; and clause (b) imposes no nonvanishing requirement on $F$.

The minimal cases are admitted by the Definition: clause (c) allows $N=1$, clause (b) allows $d=1$, clause (a) allows a single-entry run description, and the companion counterexample instantiates a one-point record.

Degenerate structures are explicit in the Definition: the parameter set $\Theta$ may be a singleton, $F$ may be constant, $S$ may contain one preparation index, and clause (d) allows $Z$ to be any nonempty set of instrument-output values.

The Definition uses closed boxes $[z_j-\varepsilon_j,z_j+\varepsilon_j]$ with $\varepsilon_j\ge0$, and clause (e) states its total bound for the closed interval $[\hat y-B,\hat y+B]$; no open-box or interior-only reading is defined.
No choice principle is used in the Definition: clauses (a)-(e) form finite tuples and finite products and evaluate maps pointwise, as clause (g) records explicitly.

The Definition contains no biconditional claim: condition $(*)$ in clause (b) is a declared interpretation obligation to be checked when a model is used, and the remaining clauses are specifications, so there is no forward implication direction to discharge.

For the same reason the Definition asserts no reverse implication; the only conditional obligation it introduces is the reviewer-facing condition $(*)$, which is checked directly against the cited framework items.

The statement names each of its four search destinations individually and asserts no existence of reports for any destination, so an empty retrieval result for a destination would not falsify any clause; no conclusion of the statement depends on a destination family being nonempty.

The statement carries no computed zero; its only numerical attribution is the recorded reported estimate of the experiment item, and the queue clauses concern retrieval status rather than arithmetic, so no vanishing quantity enters.

The statement treats the one-report branch in clause (i): one destination branch now has its primary report read, while the remaining families stay queued, and clause (vi) limits the item to a status pointer.

The statement draws no mathematical conclusion whose validity could be threatened by degeneracy; it records destinations and qualifications, and no configuration, parameter or coincidence assumption is made anywhere in it.
The statement asserts no interval, limit or boundary property; its qualification clauses concern what future records must carry rather than the behaviour of any quantity at an endpoint.

The statement selects nothing from a family of nonempty sets: the four destinations are named explicitly, the retrieved report is identified by its bibliographic description, and no collective selection is asserted.

The statement asserts no biconditional; its implications are one-directional qualifications, for instance that a future experiment record requires a retrieved primary report (clause iii), and no converse is claimed.

No reverse implication is asserted either: clause (iv) of the statement records that the comparison obligation is supplied for the specified report, which is a status statement about one branch and not a converse of any clause.

(b) On the positive rectangle the quotient nu_a nu_p/(nu_1 nu_2) is increasing in the numerators and decreasing in the denominators by the order rules, the quotient is positive, and the strictly increasing square root preserves the two inequalities giving the displayed bounds; the indicated admissible corners attain both endpoints.

(c) D_l(a)<=k holds exactly when |zhat_j-P_{l,j}(a)|<=k u_j for every j, which by u_j>0 is exactly the coordinatewise interval condition; taking preimages gives S_l(k)=P_l^{-1}(prod_j[zhat_j-k u_j,zhat_j+k u_j]), a deterministic arithmetic comparison with no probability model.

(d) The two waves propagate along +-e_1, so the Doppler factors are gamma(1-beta) and gamma(1+beta); identifying the rest-frame readings with the rest transition frequencies gives nu_1=gamma(1-beta)nu_p and nu_2=gamma(1+beta)nu_a, whence nu_a nu_p/(nu_1 nu_2)=1 and Q_SR=0; replacing gamma by one gives Q_1(beta)=(1-beta^2)^{-1/2}-1.

With zhat=15/10^10 and u=23/10^10, Q_SR=0 gives D_SR=15/23<1, so zero lies in the descriptive band [-8/10^10,38/10^10]; for beta=169/500 the exact comparisons (531/500)^2*(221439/250000)<1<(1063/1000)^2*(221439/250000) give 31/500<Q_1<63/1000, hence D_1>10^7, so the SR prediction meets the k=1 criterion while the specified Gamma=1 alternative fails it at the nominal speed.

Synthesis and scope: (a)-(d) follow from steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 with the displayed identities; the comparisons are conditional on declared hard bounds and admissible tuples, are not instantiated by the experiment's 1-sigma scales, yield no p-value, coverage or rejection rate and no proof or unique validation of SR, and inherit every apparatus, calibration, finite-sampling and unpublished-covariance qualification.

boundaries.evidence: The products over $j$ in parts (a) and (c) are finite products over the fixed index set $\{1,\dots,m\}$ with $m=Nd\ge1$, and step 1.1 shows the box is nonempty; emptiness of $C_\ell$ is not an exception but the exclusion conclusion the theorem analyses, and it is treated by the sufficient disjointness criterion of step 2.1.

Zero is treated on both sides: e=0 makes B(z,e) the singleton {z} in step 1.1, k=0 makes S_l(0) the preimage of the point zhat in step 1.3, and the denominators are strictly positive (positive frequency intervals in step 1.2, u_j>0 in step 1.3, and gamma^2(1-beta)(1+beta)=1 in step 1.4), so no division by zero arises.

The one-dimensional and one-point cases are included: m=Nd with N=d=1 is allowed in part (a), k=1 is the criterion instantiated in part (d), and step 2.2 evaluates the single reported estimate u pair at the nominal beta.

Degeneracies are explicit: the noise-free hard-bound case e=0 gives a singleton box (step 1.1), the zero multiplier k=0 gives the point preimage (step 1.3), and the alternative hypothesis Gamma(1) is a deliberately degenerate time-dilation factor held apart from the SR model.

Endpoints are attained and used: step 1.2 attains both propagated endpoints at corners of the rectangle, step 1.3 uses closed intervals with the closed k criterion, and step 2.2 evaluates the closed descriptive band [-8/10^10,38/10^10] at its nominal beta.

No choice principle is used: A_l, P_l and the records are declared data, the maxima in part (c) are finite comparisons by recursion, the propagated bounds are attained at named corners in step 1.2, and no selection from a family of nonempty sets occurs anywhere.

The Statement's biconditionals are discharged direction by direction: in step 1.1, if C_l is nonempty then a chosen admissible tuple has its prediction in B(z,e), so the image meets the box, and conversely a point of the intersection gives an element of C_l; in step 1.3 the bound D_l(a)<=k gives every coordinate inequality.

The reverse directions are discharged in the same steps: in step 1.3 the coordinatewise interval inequalities imply the maximum bound D_l(a)<=k because k is compared coordinate by coordinate, and in step 1.1 membership of a prediction in the box gives membership of the tuple in the preimage C_l.

setup.evidence: Setup authored from the primary report pp. 2-3 and Figure 1: Penning source, 58.6 MeV/u acceleration, ESR storage, electron cooling, reported spreads, stored-ion numbers and metastable fraction, the Lambda system and the three laser wavelengths; journal literature locators retained in the sources field.

procedure.evidence: Procedure records the iodine/Rb-referenced laser chain with SHG and offset lock, the fiber transport, the 20 microrad/50 micrometre stage accuracy, the 80 microrad overlap scrapers, the four 100-microsecond counter cycle, dark/background subtraction, the OODR same-velocity-class selection, the 81-point scan with pause at 69, and the 40 fitted spectra; unpublished raw data, weights and covariance are stated as unavailable.

observations.evidence: Observations quote exactly the Table I frequencies (546455143.0, 546474960.7, 384225534.98, 777210326.98 MHz) and Eq (4) epsilon=(1.5+/-2.3)e-9 at nominal beta=0.338; the derived 1.4744849565e-9 from the rounded centers was recomputed and matches; rest-frequency inputs are attributed to references 21-22 of the report and not claimed retrieved.

uncertainty.evidence: Uncertainty budget reported exactly as labelled 1-sigma: aggregate 0.43/1.6/1.25 MHz, all antiparallel and parallel contributions, the 0.44+/-1.0 MHz Gouy correction, the 0.5 MHz linearization assignment and the excess-linewidth attribution; no independence, Gaussian law, covariance or coverage is invented.

interpretation.evidence: Interpretation separates the reported estimate from prediction: the observable tests the combined Doppler, atomic-transition and apparatus assumptions; the |alpha|<=2.0e-8 quotation is recorded as the source sensitivity statement, and RMS/SME and future prospects are marked contextual; no significance or framework proof is asserted.

sources.evidence: The source is the retrieved five-page primary report arXiv:1409.7951v1 (PDF sha256 prefix d40420de81cf93d3, 454448 bytes), matching the coverage retrieval stamp; every quoted value is traceable to Eqs (1)-(4), Figures 1-2 and Table I.

statistical_inference.evidence: The record states that the 0.6 MHz entry is a weighted-fit statistical uncertainty over forty spectra rather than forty independent readings, does not invent a likelihood or coverage, keeps reported standard scales distinct from hard bounds, and asserts no rejection or significance claim anywhere.
